- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < 0.33) and model shows gradual upward trend, reduce forecast slope; price may not rebound as expected.
- After sharp downward spikes in true outcome, model often overcorrects upward — cap forecast rise to 1–2% above prior peak if sentiment remains bearish.
- If official event net supply is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model tends to underpredict downside — add 1–3% buffer below forecast for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model often fails to adjust — force a 1–2 day lagged mean reversion correction if true outcome drops >5% from prior peak.
- For multi-day auction events (e.g., CAP3 EU), model overestimates price stability — reduce forecast by 1–2% per auction day if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows volatility, assume sentiment is misaligned — adjust forecast to reflect 1–2% volatility band around historical mean for next 3 days.
